newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks in late upswing on inflation, Dow.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks in late upswing on inflation, Dow.

text.p: Mexican stocks reversed their earlier slump to end ahead on Monday prompted by inflation that was below expectations and a late rally on Wall Street, traders and analysts said.

"It seems to us the bourse has strong support between 3,750 and 3,800 points. The bourse recovered on slightly better-than-expected inflation figures which pave the way for a downward trend in Cetes rates," said Lars Schonander, head of equity research at Santander Investment in Mexico City.
The leading IPC share index ended up 18.09 points, or 0.48 percent, at 3,827.99.
Trading volume was slow at 60.1 million shares, but improved on earlier dealing.
Banco de Mxico announced in late trade that consumer prices rose by 0.66 percent in the first half of March, less than an average 0.71 percent forecast in a Reuters survey MXAAP.
A Reuters survey of nine Mexico City money market traders showed they predict bellwether 28-day Cetes rates will fall by an average of 66 basis points to 21.04 percent at today's auction.

"We were very encouraged when the Dow took off. It seems the good news is the U.S. Federal Open Market Committee will only raise base rates 25 basis points, which is already discounted," a Mexico City floor trader said.
The FOMC meeting will be held on Tuesday.
The Dow Jones meanwhile surged 1.48 percent to close at 6,905.25 points.
Traders said dealing was very slow for most of the session ahead of Easter holidays on March 27 and 28.
"The market will be in the doldrums this week. Most dealers are on vacation, and those left behind are not doing much," a dealer said.

Benchmark Telmex, which accounted for one-third of all trade, dragged the IPC down for most of the session. Telmex L shares ended off 10 centavos at 15.70 pesos, while its ADRs ended flat at 39-7/8 on Wall Street.
"Most trading was in Telmex. Its price was fixed by foreign traders on Friday when we were closed, so all we did was adjust in line with the change when we opened again today," the dealer added.
Traders noted Telmex ADRs fell sharply at the end of last week.
"A convert was issued against it, so they hedged against the convert price," a New York trader said.
On the broad market, 103 stocks changed hands, of which gains outnumbered declines by 44 to 34.
Traders said the most influential leading gainer was holding company Femsa, which gained 1.30 pesos to 35.30 pesos.
"Femsa hauled the market up to a degree, after all it is a blue chip and is still a gem for investors," a trader said.
Financial group Abaco headed the leading decliners on what some analysts said were concerns over the firm's finances.
(( --Karina Balderas, Mexico City newsroom +525 728-7907))
